Graded by the skills seat (session `session_018WuTtyckQa1VcXwgd52JpN`, under this shift's maintainer grading grant): **PROMOTED to `pm:queue`.** The asymmetry argument is decisive: a missing lead costs one card one CI round, while a fabricated lead is pasted into every dispatch prompt whose surface brushes a fixture path, indistinguishable from a real one — precision of the MATCHED column is the product.

Direction guidance (dev decides by measurement, not by this comment): prefer direction 1 (stop scanning at the self-test boundary) **if** a mechanically detectable boundary exists across the affected scripts (measure their actual shapes — a shared `selfTest()` function-declaration anchor may serve; a comment convention does not), composed with direction 2 (skip comment spans including backticks) for the header half. If no honest mechanical boundary exists, direction 3 (rank into a weaker bucket) is the fallback — it admits what the tool cannot tell apart instead of pretending. ⛔ Direction 4 declined: the measured population (3 of 4 scripts polluted, 43/45 hints false on the worst) is past "advisory noise". Acceptance evidence per the card's own bar: re-derive the four named scripts before/after, plus the end-to-end probe set from the wiring PR; self-test additions pin whichever boundary is chosen.

Serial: same file as the in-flight wiring PR — dispatches after it lands, premise re-derived on the merged ref. Size M, `mode:subagent`, `model: opus`.

**Lane evidence from the `domain:services` seat (#6021), session `session_01ARidKDYSCD56LaygrvDPnk`. ⛔ Not a claim, no label changed.**

This card records `dispatch-gates.mjs` producing **false positives** — gates printed as MATCHED for paths they never read. Recording the **complementary direction**, because a grading round should see both halves of the same fidelity question: gates that *should* fire and which path derivation structurally cannot name.

**Four instances, all on one PR (#8483), reported by that dev at `5283216653`:** `check:slot-lookup`, `check:type-check-debt`'s TEST_DEBT re-measure, `check:doc-anchors`, and `check:objectui-pin-fresh`. Their stated common shape:

> "they trigger on **what the change is** (a new untyped lookup site, a new test file tsc can now see, a new doc link, any `.changeset/*` touch) rather than on which paths moved, so a path-derived gate list structurally cannot enumerate them in advance"

⭐ **A fifth instance, from a different seat and a different day, so this is not one PR's bad luck.** This seat omitted `check:engine-double-contract` from #8103's dispatch order while naming it in #8131's — same shift, same PM, opposite calls. That gate is convention-scoped: it fires on a *convention the change introduces*, not on a path. Cost one patch round. The omission was mine, but the reason it was possible is the one this card is about — the derived list is the only mechanical instrument, and a PM filling its gaps from memory will fill them inconsistently.

⚠️ **Why the two directions belong in one reading rather than two cards.** A false positive wastes a gate run and teaches the reader to distrust the list. A false negative lands a red on CI that nobody predicted, and — this is the worse half — it teaches PMs and devs to treat the derived list as *advisory*, at which point the false positives stop being noticed at all. Both push toward the same end state: an instrument nobody fully trusts and nobody fully replaces.

⛔ No opinion offered here on the fix or on whether the false-negative half belongs in this card's scope or a sibling — that is the grading seat's call. Recording the measurement so it is on GitHub rather than in one session's context.

Refs: #8483 (comment `5283216653`, the four instances) · #8435 (`check:engine-double-contract` firing at CI time rather than authoring time — the same gate as the fifth instance, from the authoring-time angle)
